text: sugar's one twelve so it's not her sugar. she's got slurred speech and a left facial droop, husband says she was normal at six this morning. she takes metformin and warfarin
notes: cat=other_mismatch. Normal glucose + focal deficits: stroke keys apply. Slurred: no RACE aphasia. The meds sentence has a new subject -> medic.

text: her son was right there when it started he called us right away
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. 'it' has no symptom word; the dispatch supplies the stroke context. Son was present at onset = witnessed; the person named is the source (§5b).

dispatch: Possible stroke, 88 yo female, nursing facility
text: Charge nurse says she was at baseline at the 0200 check and she found her like this at 0600. Right facial droop, right arm is flaccid. She's a DNR, we have the POLST. Heading to St. Luke's, about fifteen out.
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. 'at baseline' = normal -> LKW. 0600 discovery time: no fact. Flaccid = arm 2. 'about fifteen out' -> ETA 15.

dispatch: Fall, 81 yo female, caller is daughter
text: Okay, this isn't what it came in as. She's got a right facial droop, her right arm drifts, and her speech is garbled. Daughter says she was fine at seven p.m.
notes: cat=other_mismatch. Fall dispatch but the words describe a stroke: stroke keys apply (§4c second half). Garbled: G.F.A.S.T. only.

text: Unwitnessed. Last known well two fifteen this afternoon per the patient's wife. Transporting to Mercy General, ETA twelve.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. 'per the wife' governs only the LKW sentence. 'this afternoon' adds pm.

text: Right leg drifts down, uh, both arms are strong. Onset was thirty minutes ago, witnessed by his coworkers.
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Leg drift = RACE leg 1, G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg 1 (any limb). Strong arms = RACE arm 0. Onset duration is the medic's; witnesses are coworkers = bystander.

text: shes globally aphasic wont follow commands eyes are midline temp ninety eight point six resps eighteen no allergies
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Aphasic = RACE 2. Eyes midline = gaze 0 on both scales. 98.6 F -> 37.0.

text: Last known well oh-six-thirty per the group home staff, D-stick one forty-two.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Group-home staff = caregiver -> family with job word as source (§3, §5b). Attribution governs only the LKW clause; glucose is medic.

dispatch: Chest pain, 67 yo male, cardiac history
text: Okay, sixty-seven year old male, he was fine at dinner, chest pain started around seven thirty, crushing, goes down the left arm. He took one nitro before we got here. Twelve-lead done at twenty oh four and it's attached.
notes: cat=other_tempt. symptom.onset is not a stroke key, so the chest-pain onset is labeled; 'fine at dinner' gives no LKW. Pain radiating to the arm is not a deficit. Nitro taken before EMS = home med (§4b).

dispatch: Stroke, caller states mom is 'talking funny'
text: sixty eight yom uh no wait sorry sixty eight year old female. mild droop on the right no drift speech is garbled. sugar two ninety
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Sex corrected yom -> female: only F. Mild droop = RACE 1. Unqualified 'no drift' -> G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg 0 + RACE arm 0 (§5b). Garbled: G.F.A.S.T. speech 1, no RACE (§4b).

text: wife saw him collapse at the table, he came around right away. heart rate one forty two irregular, BP ninety over sixty. He's alert now.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Collapse without neuro signs: complaint.chief, no onset_witnessed (§4c).

text: She ate shrimp at dinner, her lips are swelling up. She used her EpiPen before we got here. Allergic to shellfish, sats ninety-seven.
notes: cat=other_plain. Self-administered EpiPen before EMS = taken before arrival, like the nitro rule (§4b) -> epinephrine.

text: mail carrier found him on the porch around eleven, last time the neighbor saw him normal was about six last night
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Found by the mail carrier -> false, bystander. 'around eleven' is a discovery time: no fact (§5b). 'about six last night' -> '6 pm' (approximator dropped, last night adds pm). Neighbor = bystander. No age/sex: only in the dispatch.

text: son found him in the recliner, he's not able to speak at all and he can't lift his right arm. last seen normal by the son at two this afternoon. pressure one ninety over one oh four
facts: not able to speak at all
notes: cat=other_mismatch. Unknown-problem dispatch, stroke presentation in the same utterance: 'found' now gives onset_witnessed false. Can't speak = RACE aphasia 2.

text: Last known well eleven thirty, correction, ten thirty, per the aide.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Corrected value only (§5). Aide = caregiver -> family, source 'aide'.

text: daughter says he was fine at dinner, found him on the couch around nine, D-stick's thirty four and he's confused
notes: cat=other_tempt. Hypoglycemia: 'fine at dinner' and 'found him' give no stroke keys (§4c). Confusion -> C, not complaint.

text: He takes Plavix and, um, metformin, and the blood pressure one, lisinopril. He was fine at nine this morning, and I was right with him when his face went all crooked.
speaker: wife
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Wife on the mic. Plavix is an antiplatelet: meds.list only, no anticoagulant (§5a). Her description of the face -> deficit only, no G.F.A.S.T./RACE.

dispatch: Breathing problem, 72 yo female, COPD history
text: seventy two year old female short of breath sats eighty eight on room air put her on four liters now ninety three resps twenty eight uh she's on spiriva and albuterol
notes: cat=other_plain. Room air then oxygen: two readings, on_oxygen false and true (§4c). Spiriva = tiotropium.

text: Bicyclist hit by a car, bystanders saw the whole thing. He says he can't feel his legs, numb from the waist down. Collar's on. Pressure one ten over seventy, pulse sixty.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Mechanism counts as complaint. Suspected spinal numbness is not a stroke deficit (§4c); witnessed crash is not stroke onset.

text: Wife thinks maybe he was okay around noon? She's really not sure, she was out most of the day.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Hedged LKW ('thinks maybe', 'not sure') -> no fact (§4c).

text: forty five year old female abdominal pain since two this afternoon pulse one hundred bp one thirty over eighty temp thirty eight point one
notes: cat=other_plain. Celsius as spoken. 'this afternoon' adds pm.

text: she woke up like this. husband says she was fine when they went to bed around ten thirty last night
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. 'woke up like this' -> false (unattributed, medic). Bedtime normal -> LKW '10:30 pm' (last night adds pm, 'around' dropped). Age/sex only in dispatch: not labeled.

text: She was fine, she was totally fine at four thirty when I left for work, and then I got home at six and she was on the couch like this.
speaker: husband
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Husband on the mic. Coming home to her already 'like this' is being found (§4c 'found or woke up with symptoms') -> false. 'six' is a discovery time: no fact. No am/pm said.

text: Um, so the daughter found her in the bathroom at oh-five-twenty, and uh, she doesn't know when she was last normal.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Found -> false. 0520 is a discovery time: no time fact. Unknown LKW: no fact (§5b).

dispatch: Stroke/CVA, 70s male, left-side weakness per caller
text: Left arm and leg weakness, he can't lift the left arm off the bed, left leg drifts, face is symmetric. Last known well zero nine thirty per his daughter.
facts: can't lift the left arm off the bed
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Can't lift arm = 2, leg drift = 1. Symmetric face = 0 on both scales.

dispatch: CVA - 77 yo male - skilled nursing facility
text: Last seen normal at twenty-one hundred by the night nurse. Allergic to penicillin. Takes Eliquis and metoprolol.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Facility nurse = family, source 'nurse'. Allergy and meds are subjectless shorthand -> medic (§5b). 24-hour time kept as said.

text: RACE exam: face two, arm two, leg one, gaze one, aphasia two, RACE of eight. Last known well fourteen fifteen per his wife. BGL one twenty.
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Bare RACE item scores: RACE items + derived G.F.A.S.T. items (§4d), no deficits (§5b). The total gives nothing. Age/sex only in dispatch.

text: Wife saw the whole seizure, he was shaking all over for like two minutes. He's postictal now, only responds to voice. Took his Keppra this morning.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Witnessed seizure is not a stroke onset. Responds to voice = V. Home med taken before EMS -> meds.list (Keppra = levetiracetam), subjectless -> medic.

text: okay he's got his eyes deviated to the left, can't lift the right arm at all, and he's completely aphasic. Pressure two twenty over one twenty. He's on Coumadin.
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Can't lift = arm 2; 'aphasic' = RACE 2. Coumadin -> warfarin.

dispatch: Stroke symptoms, bus stop, bystander caller
text: the witness uh the lady at the bus stop she saw the whole thing
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Stranger who saw it = bystander; 'the whole thing' has no symptom word, stroke dispatch gives the context.

dispatch: Stroke - caller is daughter by phone, patient home alone
text: daughter was on the phone with him not video just the phone so she didn't actually see anything she says he was fine at like eight fifteen this morning
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Phone only, 'didn't see anything' -> not witnessed, but it is not 'nobody saw it'/found either, so no onset_witnessed fact (§4c, §5b). LKW 8:15 am ('like' dropped, 'this morning' adds am).

dispatch: Possible stroke, caller is patient's daughter (remote)
text: I was on FaceTime with her and I watched it happen, it was, like, ten after one.
speaker: daughter
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Daughter on the mic. Seeing it on a video call counts as witnessed (§5b). Clock time of a witnessed onset is symptom.onset, not LKW (§4). 'like' dropped.

text: Okay so, uh, wife says he was fine at twenty to four, that's the last time she saw him normal.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. 'twenty to four' = 3:40; no am/pm said, so none added.

dispatch: Sick person, 90 yo female, home caregiver on scene
text: Generalized weakness since eight this morning, not eating. Caregiver says she was her usual self yesterday. Temp one-oh-one point two, heart rate one-oh-eight.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Generalized (not focal) weakness is not a stroke deficit. 'usual self yesterday' gives no LKW. 101.2 F -> 38.4 C. symptom.onset keeps 'since' (§5b).

text: son says dad was normal at 0745 when he dropped off groceries, he came back at nine thirty and found him in the chair
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Son is the one who came back and found him -> false, source son. 9:30 is a discovery time: no fact.

dispatch: Possible stroke, apartment complex, caller is building manager
text: Uh, last known well is unknown. Building super found him down in his apartment. Sats ninety-four on two liters.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. 'LKW unknown' gives no fact (§5b). Found by the building superintendent -> false; super is a bystander, not a caregiver. 'found down' is not repeated as complaint.chief (structured key holds it).

text: Found in her backyard, nobody's seen her since this morning. Core temp ninety-one point four, shivering, responds to pain only.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Hypothermia: 'found' / 'nobody's seen her' give no stroke keys (§4c). 91.4 F -> 33.0 C. Hypothermia is held by vitals.temp, so no complaint.

text: lkw 1340 per coworker she was with her in the break room when it started
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Coworker is a bystander (not family/caregiver). Present when it started -> witnessed.

text: Okay, uh, we're gonna get him over onto the stretcher, give us a second.
notes: cat=other_plain. Crew talk, no facts.

text: Roommate says he overdosed on heroin, found him on the bathroom floor, last saw him okay around 2200. Pinpoint pupils, resps six, sats eighty-one. Narcan given, now he's breathing twelve.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Roommate = bystander. 'last saw him okay' is not a LKW here (not stroke-like). Narcan is an EMS intervention: no meds.list. Before/after readings are two facts (§4c).

text: hes got right sided weakness and slurred speech wife says it started at 7 15 while they were eating she saw it
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Weakness without severity: G.F.A.S.T. 1, no RACE. Slurred = dysarthria: speech 1, no RACE aphasia (§5a). '7 15' -> '7:15'; 'she saw it' is the wife.

dispatch: Stroke/CVA, 74 yo F, caller reports facial droop
text: Seventy-four year old female, left facial droop, uh, left arm drift. Speech is clear. Husband says she was fine at one fifty.
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Unqualified droop = RACE facial 2. 'Speech is clear' = G.F.A.S.T. speech 0, no RACE value (§5b). Only LKW is the husband's.

text: Patient states it feels like an elephant sitting on his chest. He's allergic to sulfa and codeine. He's a full code.
notes: cat=other_plain. The complaint is the patient's description; allergies and code status are the medic's sentences.

dispatch: Stroke/CVA - caller is wife, symptoms may have resolved
text: wife says he was slurring his words at dinner but it cleared up. speech is clear now face symmetric no drift. one fifty two over eighty eight pulse seventy six
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Resolved finding: current state wins and it is not a deficit (§5b), so no stroke.deficits. 'at dinner' is not a LKW (no 'fine/normal at').

text: Um, neighbor found him on the kitchen floor. He says he fell going to the bathroom and couldn't get back up. Nobody saw it. He's alert, knows where he is.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Found-down fall: 'found' and 'nobody saw it' give no onset_witnessed outside a stroke dispatch (§4c).

text: Her face started drooping on one side and her words were all mixed up. I was right there with her when it started.
speaker: daughter
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Family description of findings -> deficits only, never RACE/G.F.A.S.T. (§5b).

text: onset witnessed by the wife at 1805 glucose one oh one hes on zarelto
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Clock time of a witnessed onset -> symptom.onset. 'zarelto' is ASR for Xarelto = rivaroxaban. One drug word, two facts: anticoagulant first (§5b).

text: Patient states she was fine when she sat down to watch the news at six thirty. Now she's got left-sided numbness and weakness. Alert and oriented times four. Denies blood thinners. NKDA.
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. LKW is the patient's; the new sentence is the medic's. Weakness (any side) = G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg 1, no RACE. Subjectless 'Denies blood thinners'/NKDA are the medic's (§5b).

dispatch: Possible stroke, adult male, caller is neighbor
text: Nobody was with him when it happened, he lives by himself. Pressure's two-oh-four over one-ten, pulse ninety-two and irregular.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. 'Nobody was with him when it happened' = nobody saw it -> false (§5b). 'two-oh-four' = 204.

text: Mom heard a noise and found her seizing in bed, lasted maybe three minutes, says she was fine at bedtime. History of epilepsy, on Lamictal.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Seizure call: 'found' and 'fine at bedtime' give nothing. Subjectless 'on lamictal' is the medic's (§4c); Lamictal = lamotrigine. Age only in dispatch.

text: Staff found her on the floor next to the bed at 0540, she was fine at the 0400 rounds. No injuries, alert and oriented, sugar ninety-six.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Found-down fall with no injury: no stroke keys; 'found on the floor' alone is not stated as a complaint.

text: eighty four year old female slipped and fell in the bathroom aide found her on the floor at the 0300 rounds says she was fine at the midnight check. right leg is shortened and rotated
notes: cat=other_tempt. Found-down fall: no onset_witnessed, no LKW (§4c). Shortened/rotated leg is trauma, not a deficit.

text: Correction on that pressure, it's one eighty-four over ninety-six, not one forty-eight. Uh, and he's on Pradaxa. ETA eight minutes to Regional.
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. Only the corrected BP; 'not one forty-eight' is a rejected value. Stroke dispatch but no stroke keys stated.

text: Wife heard a thump from the garage, went out there and found him on the floor, that was maybe twenty minutes ago.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Hearing a thump is not seeing it (§4c), but she found him -> false. '20 minutes ago' dates the discovery and is hedged: no time fact.

text: He was fine at lunch, and when I came back from the store at three he was like this. He's type one, he has an insulin pump.
speaker: wife
notes: cat=other_tempt. Wife on the mic. Diabetic call, no stroke-like words: no LKW, no onset_witnessed. Insulin pump -> insulin (§4c).

text: the store manager saw him pass out in the checkout line he was out maybe ten seconds. alert and oriented now pressure one oh four over sixty two pulse fifty two
notes: cat=other_tempt. Syncope, no neuro signs: no onset_witnessed. Store manager = bystander (§4c).

dispatch: Stroke, 59 yo male, gym, bystander caller
text: fifty nine year old male collapsed on the treadmill right sided weakness eyes deviated to the left sats ninety eight room air pulse one ten gym staff saw him go down
notes: cat=stroke_mixed. 'collapsed' is a presenting problem with no structured key -> complaint.chief (§4c). Gym staff are bystanders, not caregivers (§4c).

dispatch: Fall with head injury, 79 yo male
text: Witnessed fall down about six stairs, son saw it happen, hit his head on the landing. GCS fifteen, motor six. He's on Eliquis.
notes: cat=other_tempt. Witnessed trauma is not stroke onset (§4c). GCS total gives no ACVPU letter (§4c); motor 6 is labeled.

dispatch: Seizure, 58 yo male, caller is wife
text: No seizure activity that we saw. He has left-sided weakness, can't lift the left arm, and his eyes are deviated to the right. Wife watched it start at fifteen twenty while they were talking.
notes: cat=other_mismatch. Seizure dispatch, stroke presentation: witnessed onset with clock time -> onset_witnessed + symptom.onset (§4). 'fifteen twenty' -> '15:20'.

text: Witnessed onset. BP one seventy-eight over ninety-four, heart rate eighty-eight, sats ninety-six on room air.
notes: cat=stroke_nosym. Stroke dispatch makes the bare 'Witnessed onset' a stroke.onset_witnessed fact (§4c run E rule). Unattributed, so medic.
